question: According to the Census of India 2011, what is the percentage of India's population that live in urban areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __31.16__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The total urban population in the country as per Census 2011 is more than 377 million** forming 31.16% of the total population.**
 
• The data shows that Goa is the most **urbanized state with 62.17% of the population living in urban areas**. But if one goes by geographical area and total population, Tamil Nadu is the most urbanized state followed by Kerala (47.7 percent) upstaging Maharashtra (45.2 percent)
 
• The total rural population in the country as per the census of 2011 is 833.1 million. 
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh becomes the most rural state with **89.97 percent of the rural population followed by Bihar.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The responsibility of conducting the decennial Census rests with the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• Census of India 2011 is the 15th census conducted in India, which is the largest democratic country in the world.
 
• The census data is collected every 10 years, and it provides important information about the population, literacy rate, occupation, and other demographic factors.
 
• The percentage of India's population that lives in urban areas has been increasing over the years due to various factors such as urbanization, industrialization, and modernization.
 
• According to the 2011 census, the percentage of India's population living in urban areas is 31.16% which is a significant increase from the previous census in 2001.
 
• Urbanization has both positive and negative impacts on society, and it is important to manage it effectively to ensure sustainable development.
